The base, located west of Fallujah on a route once known as the "road of death" during the American invasion of Iraq, houses both Iraqi forces and members of the Popular Mobilisation Force, some of whom are Iran-backed militias.

Iraqis fear being dragged into a war not of their making as both sides escalate attacks.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
In this episode of This is America, hosted by Anna Burns-Francis, Al Jazeera examines the deepening divide in US media amid the war with Iran. The Trump administration intensifies attacks on mainstream outlets, accusing them of spreading "fake news" and undermining war messaging, while Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth told reporters "you're either informing the people of the truth or you're not." Trust in traditional media has sharply declined—from around 70% in the late 1970s to just 28% last year—while social media overtook television as Americans' top news source for the first time, with 54% of people now getting news online.
Chief US correspondent Alan Fisher reported from the White House that right-wing influencers with hard passes now amplify the president's message, as traditional outlets face restricted access. The programme explored the rise of alternative platforms: Joe Rogan's podcast draws 14 million listeners per episode; Tucker Carlson, Megyn Kelly and Dan Bongino command
title: US media divide deepens over Iran war narrative | This is America

Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz is disrupting approximately 30 percent of global energy supplies, including oil, gas and fertilisers critical to world agriculture. The GCC has warned that Tehran is now charging vessels for passage through the waterway, which Al Etaibi says violates international law guaranteeing freedom of navigation. 

Mortazavi suggests the White House underestimated Iran's capacity to weaponise the strait, despite warnings from regional allies. The blockade's effects are expected to ripple through global supply chains in the coming months, impacting countries from Australia to Kenya.
